subject: Request: Tailored availability promise + hot-standby plan for NorthWind Labs
messages:
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@northwind.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: NorthWind Procurement <procurement@northwind.ai>
Subject: Availability ask for GA launch - NorthWind

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team has one final gating item before the GA rollout: NorthWind is requesting a written availability promise tied to a hot-standby plan for our production inference traffic. We're asking for: a written availability commitment for the primary region (us-west) at p99 availability 99.95% for the month, plus a documented hot-standby failover procedure and SLA-backed fallback to a warm region.

Key constraints:
- We cannot tolerate more than 20 minutes of customer-facing downtime during an incident.
- We require a documented RTO & RPO for KV cache restore for their session-based workloads.
- Procurement wants a single-line item for the availability commitment we can reference in the contract.

Can Redwood provide a tailored promise and a short ops runbook? If useful, I attached our high-level launch window and traffic estimates.

Best,
Emily
Emily Cho
Director of Platform Engineering, NorthWind Labs
(emily.cho@northwind.ai)

Team — forwarding NorthWind's ask. High-level: they want a written availability promise + hot-standby runbook and RTO/RPO for KV cache. We can propose a tailored commitment but need to align on product constraints, cost delta, and legal acceptability.

Questions for initial triage:
1) Karthik — can the serving runtime guarantee p99 availability at 99.95% for a single region with warm failover to a second region (us-east)? What are the operational caveats (e.g., warm replica capacity, state sync for KV cache, expected failover window)?
2) Marcus — procurement will want this codified with an operational runbook and on-call commitments. Do we have a standard hot-standby runbook we can adapt? What side-effects on our capacity commitments (reserved pools) do we need?
3) Laura — pricing: this will almost certainly be a committed capacity + SLA add-on. What's the recommended pricing approach (monthly uplift vs one-time readiness fee)?

I've attached the customer's proposal for context. Prefer quick sync if helpful — I can host a 30-min call today.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@northwind.ai>
Subject: Re: Fwd: Availability ask for GA launch - NorthWind

Olga — quick notes from infra/product POV.

Summary: Technically feasible with caveats.
- We can operate a warm-standby in us-east with KV cache snapshotting and incremental sync, but warm capacity must be sized ~30-40% of peak to meet the 20-minute outage cap during failover (we'd need accelerated cache warming on failover).
- Expected failover window: nominally 10-25 minutes (detection + DNS propagation + cache warm). Best-case ~10m with aggressive pre-warming and traffic steering; worst-case up to 25m depending on external DNS TTLs and customer routing.
- RTO/RPO: we can guarantee RTO of 20 minutes if the customer accepts a managed cache-warm approach and we maintain dedicated warm nodes (cost uplift). RPO depends on snapshot cadence — with near-real-time replication (every 5 minutes) we can offer RPO <= 5 minutes.
- Risk: cross-region network partition could complicate KV recovery; we need runbook steps to validate session integrity.

Operational needs:
- Dedicated warm pool in us-east pre-allocated for NorthWind during launch windows.
- A documented ops playbook: detection triggers, promote/redirect steps, cache health checks, rollback criteria.

I'll draft a one-page ops summary and a short list of runbook steps. This will need Marcus to sign off on readiness SLA and capacity hold.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachment: hot-standby-ops-checklist.xlsx (planned)

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Cho <emily.cho@northwind.ai>
Subject: Re: Fwd: Availability ask for GA launch - NorthWind

Thanks team. Agree with Karthik's technical summary. A few operational and commercial points:

1) Capacity hold: We can reserve a warm pool sized at 35% of projected peak during the initial 60-day GA window, then revisit. That requires a reserved capacity commitment in the contract (monthly commit).

2) SLA language: Legal will need a simple measurable SLA clause. Suggested wording: "Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.95% p99 availability for the primary jurisdiction and provide documented failover procedures and RTO/RPO guarantees as set forth in the runbook." We should avoid unlimited penalties; propose a credit schedule capped at one month's committed fees per quarter.

3) On-call: We can provide a named escalation contact and 24/7 on-call for the first 30 days post-launch as part of a launch readiness fee. After that, standard incident response applies.

Laura — please propose pricing options: (A) monthly uplift (recommended) for reserved warm pool + (B) one-time readiness fee to cover runbook automation and playbook drills.

Once we have pricing and a 1-page ops summary, I'll feed this into Legal for a short addendum.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Availability ask for GA launch - NorthWind

Hi all — pricing options for NorthWind based on the technical/ops constraints below. Numbers are illustrative; final T&Cs to be tied to committed capacity.

Option A (Monthly uplift - recommended):
- Reserved warm pool (35% of projected peak): $18,000/month
- SLA add-on (availability promise + named on-call for 30 days): $6,000/month
- Total uplift: $24,000/month (added to their committed host fees)

Option B (One-time readiness):
- One-time readiness fee (runbook automation, drills, named on-call setup): $45,000 (covers first 60 days)
- Reduced monthly uplift thereafter (reserved pool only): $15,000/month

SLA penalties: capped credits equal to 100% of one month's uplift per quarter for SLA misses tied to Redwood operational failures. We shouldn't accept uncapped liabilities.

Next steps: if NorthWind accepts Option A, we prepare a 1-page addendum (ops summary + pricing line items) and route to Legal. Marcus — please confirm runbook checklist and RTO/RPO language; Karthik — can you attach the 1-page ops summary to the addendum once done?

Olga — happy to take lead on the addendum draft and coordinate signatures.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Commercial Pricing — Redwood Inference
